reader_answers.evidence: Run2 case109 NEW frozen answer Q1: At the running bot’s address, choose Use the shared NomNomzBot app and Next; no Client ID or Client Secret is needed. Skip Bot account, then skip Spotify, Discord and YouTube. On the final card, skipped services may remain Not set; choose Finish setup, then sign in as the broadcaster to connect the channel. No extra services, separate bot login/account or TTS setup are needed. Independent source check: Explicit Use shared app, Next, skip four optional steps, Finish setup and broadcaster sign-in. Resolved default Client ID alone not decision. Run2 case109 NEW frozen answer Q2: A separate bot Twitch account, Twitch Client Secret and healthy Event feed are all unnecessary for first sign-in. The new bot has no broadcaster connection for an event-feed check yet. If registering your own Twitch app instead, you cannot proceed with registration while email is unverified or two-factor authentication is off: verify email and enable two-factor authentication first. The article establishes this in Use your own Twitch app and links Twitch’s registration requirements; I have not consulted that external page. You can still take the shared-app path now. Independent source check: No separate bot account, Client Secret or healthy feed needed; own-app registrant must verify email and enable2FA before registering. Article own-app instructions attribute this to Twitch; URL reproduction not required. Sign in as broadcaster afterward to connect the channel. Saving Spotify credentials only prepares its account connection and music features; it does not link the individual account or choose a playback device. Those still need configuration afterward.
